```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(BSDA)
```

```{r}
data <- read_csv("~/Data Science Toolbox/sprint1/hotel_bookings_clean.csv")

train <- subset(data, split == "train")
validation <- subset(data, split == "validation")
test <- subset(data, split == "test")
```

```{r}
model <- glm(
  is_canceled ~ hotel +
    lead_time +
    deposit_type +
    market_segment +
    adr +
    customer_type +
    total_of_special_requests +
    previous_cancellations +
    arrival_date_month +
    is_repeated_guest,
  data = train,
  family = binomial
)

summary(model)
```

```{r}
model <- glm(
  is_canceled ~ lead_time + hotel,
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)
```

```{r}
model_logit <- glm(
  formula(model),
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

model_probit <- glm(
  formula(model),
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "probit")
)

model_cloglog <- glm(
  formula(model),
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "cloglog")
)
```

```{r}
models <- list(
  Logit = model_logit,
  Probit = model_probit,
  Cloglog = model_cloglog
)

results <- sapply(models, function(m) {
  p <- predict(m, validation, type = "response")
  mean((p - validation$is_canceled)^2)
})

print(results)
```

```{r}
# Transform lead_time
model_log_lead <- update(
  model_logit,
  . ~ . - lead_time + log1p(lead_time)
)

# Predict on validation data
p_log_lead <- predict(
  model_log_lead,
  newdata = validation,
  type = "response"
)

# Calculate Brier score
brier_log_lead <- mean(
  (p_log_lead - validation$is_canceled)^2
)

# Compare to original
c(
  Original = results["Logit"],
  Log_lead = brier_log_lead
)
```

```{r}
# Columns we don't want to use as predictors
exclude <- c(
  "is_canceled",
  "split",
  "arrival_date",
  "arrival_date_year",
  "total_nights",
  "total_guests",
  "has_agent"
)

# Select all remaining predictors
predictors <- setdiff(names(train), exclude)

# Construct the full model formula
full_formula <- reformulate(
  predictors,
  response = "is_canceled"
)

# Fit the full logistic regression
model_full <- glm(
  full_formula,
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

summary(model_full)
```

```{r}
plot_cancellation <- function(variable) {

  summary_data <- train %>%
    group_by(category = .data[[variable]]) %>%
    summarise(
      cancellation_rate = mean(is_canceled),
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(n >= 100)

  ggplot(
    summary_data,
    aes(
      x = reorder(category, cancellation_rate),
      y = cancellation_rate
    )
  ) +
    geom_col() +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Cancellation rate by", variable),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Cancellation rate"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r}
# Predict probabilities on validation data
p1 <- predict(model1, newdata = validation, type = "response")
p2 <- predict(model2, newdata = validation, type = "response")

# Calculate Brier scores
brier1 <- mean((p1 - validation$is_canceled)^2)
brier2 <- mean((p2 - validation$is_canceled)^2)

# Compare models
comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Original lead time", "Log-transformed lead time"),
  AIC = c(AIC(model1), AIC(model2)),
  Brier = c(brier1, brier2)
)

print(comparison)
```
transforming lead_time improves our model
consistent with the non-linear pattern observed in EDA

```{r}
# Calculate cancellation rate for each deposit type
deposit_rates <- tapply(
  train$is_canceled,
  train$deposit_type,
  mean
)

print(deposit_rates)

# Predict on validation data using training rates
p_deposit_only <- unname(
  deposit_rates[validation$deposit_type]
)

# Calculate Brier score
brier_deposit_only <- mean(
  (p_deposit_only - validation$is_canceled)^2
)

# Compare with our full regression
data.frame(
  Model = c("Deposit only", "Model 5"),
  Brier = c(brier_deposit_only, brier5)
)
```

As we added more predictors, R started giving the warning `glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred`. This suggested that some bookings were being assigned cancellation probabilities extremely close to zero or one.

This isn't necessarily a problem, as some bookings may genuinely be very easy to predict. However, it can also indicate **complete or quasi-complete separation**, where a predictor or combination of predictors almost perfectly distinguishes cancellations from non-cancellations. In these cases, some coefficient estimates may become unstable or approach infinity.

We therefore wanted to check whether our models had converged and investigate why some predictions were so extreme.

**Checking convergence**

```{r convergence-check}
data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 3", "Model 4", "Model 5"),
  Converged = c(
    model3$converged,
    model4$converged,
    model5$converged
  )
)
```

All three models converged successfully. However, convergence alone does not rule out separation, so we investigated this further using Model 5.

**Checking for separation**

```{r separation-check}
library(detectseparation)

separation_check <- glm(
  formula(model5),
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  method = detectseparation::detect_separation
)

# Check whether any coefficients have infinite estimates
any(is.infinite(coef(separation_check)))
```

The separation check returned `FALSE`, so there was no evidence of complete or quasi-complete separation in Model 5. This suggests that the warning was not caused by infinite maximum likelihood estimates in this specification, although we still needed to investigate the extreme fitted probabilities.

**Investigating deposit type**

Looking back at the model coefficients, `deposit_type` seemed particularly important. We therefore checked how cancellation rates varied between the three deposit categories.

```{r deposit-check}
deposit_summary <- train %>%
  group_by(deposit_type) %>%
  summarise(
    Bookings = n(),
    Cancellation_Rate = mean(is_canceled),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  deposit_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Cancellation rates by deposit type in the training data"
)
```

The difference is particularly striking for Non Refund bookings: approximately 99.2% were cancelled, compared with 28.6% of No Deposit bookings.

This helps explain why the regression produces some probabilities very close to one. However, this is an unusual feature of the dataset, and we need to be cautious about assuming the same relationship would hold for future bookings.

**Checking the extreme predictions**

We also looked at how many validation predictions were below 0.01 or above 0.99, and whether these very confident predictions were generally correct.

```{r extreme-predictions}
# Model 5 validation probabilities
p5 <- predict(
  model5,
  newdata = validation,
  type = "response"
)

# Identify predictions below 1% or above 99%
extreme <- p5 < 0.01 | p5 > 0.99

# Summary of extreme predictions
extreme_results <- data.frame(
  Extreme_Predictions = sum(extreme),
  Incorrect_Classifications = sum(
    (p5[extreme] >= 0.5) !=
      validation$is_canceled[extreme]
  ),
  Brier_Extreme = mean(
    (p5[extreme] - validation$is_canceled[extreme])^2
  ),
  Brier_Other = mean(
    (p5[!extreme] - validation$is_canceled[!extreme])^2
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  extreme_results,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Performance of Model 5's extreme validation predictions"
)
```

Of the 17,331 validation bookings, 2,146 received predicted probabilities below 1% or above 99%. Only 13 of these were incorrectly classified at the 0.5 threshold.

The Brier score for these extreme predictions was 0.0060, compared with 0.1496 for the remaining bookings. This suggests that most of the very confident predictions were accurate, rather than simply being a sign of a poorly fitted model.

Overall, the numerical checks gave us reasonable confidence to continue developing Model 5. We found no separation in this specification, and the extreme probabilities were generally associated with accurately predicted outcomes.

However, we still need to check how well the final model is calibrated, since being confident and correct on most of these bookings does not guarantee that all predicted probabilities are reliable. 


```{r}
#install.packages("detectseparation")
library(detectseparation)

separation_check <- glm(
  formula(model5),
  data = train,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  method = detect_separation
)

print(separation_check)
```

```{r}
# Model 5 predictions on validation data
p5 <- predict(
  model5,
  newdata = validation,
  type = "response"
)

# Identify very confident predictions
extreme <- p5 < 0.01 | p5 > 0.99

# Check how many there are
sum(extreme)

# Check how many are incorrect
sum(
  (p5[extreme] >= 0.5) !=
    validation$is_canceled[extreme]
)

# Compare Brier score for extreme vs other predictions
data.frame(
  Group = c("Extreme", "Other"),
  N = c(sum(extreme), sum(!extreme)),
  Brier = c(
    mean((p5[extreme] -
            validation$is_canceled[extreme])^2),
    mean((p5[!extreme] -
            validation$is_canceled[!extreme])^2)
  )
)
```

Ridge
```{r}
#install.packages("glmnet")  
library(glmnet)

# Use exactly the same predictors as Model 5
x_train <- model.matrix(model5)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Apply the same encoding to validation data
predictor_terms <- delete.response(terms(model5))

validation_frame <- model.frame(
  predictor_terms,
  data = validation,
  xlev = model5$xlevels
)

x_validation <- model.matrix(
  predictor_terms,
  data = validation_frame,
  contrasts.arg = model5$contrasts
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Outcome
y_train <- train$is_canceled

# Check the columns match
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(x_train), colnames(x_validation)),
  !anyNA(x_train),
  !anyNA(x_validation)
)

dim(x_train)
dim(x_validation)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Save the folds so LASSO can use exactly the same ones
foldid <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(x_train)))

ridge_cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x = x_train,
  y = y_train,
  family = "binomial",
  alpha = 0,             # Ridge regression
  foldid = foldid,
  type.measure = "mse"   # Brier score for binary outcomes
)

plot(ridge_cv)

# Best penalty strength
ridge_cv$lambda.min
```

```{r}
# Validation probabilities
p_ridge <- as.numeric(
  predict(
    ridge_cv,
    newx = x_validation,
    s = "lambda.min",
    type = "response"
  )
)

# Ridge Brier score
brier_ridge <- mean(
  (p_ridge - validation$is_canceled)^2
)

# Comparison
data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 5: Logistic", "Ridge"),
  Brier = c(brier5, brier_ridge)
)
```


```{r}
# Fit LASSO using the same cross-validation folds as Ridge
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x = x_train,
  y = y_train,
  family = "binomial",
  alpha = 1,             # LASSO
  foldid = foldid,
  type.measure = "mse"   # Brier score
)

# Plot cross-validation results
plot(lasso_cv)

# Optimal penalty
lasso_cv$lambda.min
```

evaluate on validation data
```{r}
# Predict cancellation probabilities
p_lasso <- as.numeric(
  predict(
    lasso_cv,
    newx = x_validation,
    s = "lambda.min",
    type = "response"
  )
)

)
```

```{r}
# Store the formulas of our four candidate models
cv_formulas <- list(
  Model5 = formula(model5),
  Model7 = formula(model7),
  Model10 = formula(model10),
  Model11 = formula(model11)
)

# Prepare to store out-of-fold predicted probabilities
cv_predictions <- lapply(
  cv_formulas,
  function(f) rep(NA_real_, nrow(train))
)

# Store individual fold results
cv_results <- data.frame()

# Five-fold cross-validation
for (k in 1:5) {

  # Split training data into fitting and held-out folds
  fold_train <- train[cv_fold != k, ]
  fold_valid <- train[cv_fold == k, ]

  for (name in names(cv_formulas)) {

    message("Fitting ", name, " - Fold ", k)

    # Fit the model using four folds
    fit <- glm(
      formula = cv_formulas[[name]],
      data = fold_train,
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      control = glm.control(maxit = 50)
    )

    # Predict on the held-out fold
    p <- as.numeric(
      predict(fit, newdata = fold_valid, type = "response")
    )

    # Check predictions
    stopifnot(
      fit$converged,
      length(p) == nrow(fold_valid),
      all(is.finite(p))
    )

    # Store predictions
    cv_predictions[[name]][cv_fold == k] <- p

    # Calculate fold Brier score
    fold_brier <- mean(
      (p - fold_valid$is_canceled)^2
    )

    cv_results <- rbind(
      cv_results,
      data.frame(
        Model = name,
        Fold = k,
        Brier = fold_brier
      )
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
cv_brier <- function(fml) {

  predictions <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(train))
  fold_scores <- numeric(5)

  for (k in 1:5) {

    fit <- glm(
      fml,
      data = train[cv_fold != k, , drop = FALSE],
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      control = glm.control(maxit = 50)
    )

    if (!fit$converged) {
      stop(paste("Model did not converge in fold", k))
    }

    p <- as.numeric(predict(
      fit,
      newdata = train[cv_fold == k, , drop = FALSE],
      type = "response"
    ))

    stopifnot(all(is.finite(p)))

    predictions[cv_fold == k] <- p

    fold_scores[k] <- mean(
      (p - train$is_canceled[cv_fold == k])^2
    )
  }

  c(
    CV_Brier = mean(
      (predictions - train$is_canceled)^2
    ),
    Fold_SD = sd(fold_scores)
  )
}

# Reuse Model 11's previous CV results
original <- c(
  CV_Brier = cv_summary$CV_Brier[
    cv_summary$Model == "Model11"
  ],
  Fold_SD = cv_summary$Fold_SD[
    cv_summary$Model == "Model11"
  ]
)

# Compare
comparison <- rbind(
  Model11 = original,
  Model12 = cv_brier(formula12),
  Model13 = cv_brier(formula13)
)

print(comparison)
```

log loss penalises incorrect prediction with high confidence much more severly than brier score
```{r}
# Log-loss
log_loss <- function(y, p) {

  # Avoid log(0)
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)

  -mean(
    y * log(p) +
    (1 - y) * log(1 - p)
  )
}

# ROC-AUC using ranks
roc_auc <- function(y, p) {

  n1 <- sum(y == 1)
  n0 <- sum(y == 0)

  ranks <- rank(p, ties.method = "average")

  (sum(ranks[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) /
    (n1 * n0)
}

# Compare the models
metric_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 11", "Model 14"),

  Brier = c(
    mean((p11 - validation$is_canceled)^2),
    mean((p14 - validation$is_canceled)^2)
  ),

  LogLoss = c(
    log_loss(validation$is_canceled, p11),
    log_loss(validation$is_canceled, p14)
  ),

  ROC_AUC = c(
    roc_auc(validation$is_canceled, p11),
    roc_auc(validation$is_canceled, p14)
  )
)

print(metric_comparison)
```

```{r}
calibration_stats <- function(y, p) {

  # Avoid infinite logits
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-10), 1 - 1e-10)

  logit_p <- qlogis(p)

  # Estimate calibration intercept and slope
  fit <- glm(
    y ~ logit_p,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )

  c(
    Intercept = unname(coef(fit)[1]),
    Slope = unname(coef(fit)[2])
  )
}

rbind(
  Model11 = calibration_stats(validation$is_canceled, p11),
  Model14 = calibration_stats(validation$is_canceled, p14)
)
```

```{r}
# Squared prediction errors for each model
error11 <- (as.numeric(p11) - validation$is_canceled)^2
error14 <- (as.numeric(p14) - validation$is_canceled)^2

# Positive values mean Model 14 performs better
difference <- error11 - error14

# Identify identical booking records
original_cols <- setdiff(names(data), "split")

val_group <- validation[, original_cols, drop = FALSE] %>%
  group_by(across(everything())) %>%
  group_indices()

# Aggregate errors within duplicate groups
group_errors <- data.frame(
  group = val_group,
  difference = difference
) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    total_difference = sum(difference),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Paired bootstrap
set.seed(456)

B <- 2000

boot_differences <- replicate(B, {

  sampled <- sample.int(
    nrow(group_errors),
    size = nrow(group_errors),
    replace = TRUE
  )

  sum(group_errors$total_difference[sampled]) /
    sum(group_errors$n[sampled])
})

# Original difference and 95% percentile interval
c(
  Difference = mean(difference),
  Lower_95 = unname(quantile(boot_differences, 0.025)),
  Upper_95 = unname(quantile(boot_differences, 0.975))
)
```

```{r}
# Cross-validation function for a chosen link function

cv_link <- function(link_name) {

  predictions <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(train))
  fold_scores <- numeric(5)

  for (k in 1:5) {

    message("Link: ", link_name, " | Fold: ", k)

    # Fit on four folds
    fit <- glm(
      formula14,
      data = train[cv_fold != k, , drop = FALSE],
      family = binomial(link = link_name),
      control = glm.control(maxit = 50)
    )

    if (!fit$converged) {
      stop(paste(link_name, "did not converge in fold", k))
    }

    # Predict on the held-out fold
    p <- as.numeric(predict(
      fit,
      newdata = train[cv_fold == k, , drop = FALSE],
      type = "response"
    ))

    stopifnot(all(is.finite(p)))

    predictions[cv_fold == k] <- p

    fold_scores[k] <- mean(
      (p - train$is_canceled[cv_fold == k])^2
    )
  }

  c(
    CV_Brier = mean(
      (predictions - train$is_canceled)^2
    ),
    Fold_SD = sd(fold_scores)
  )
}

# Compare with the existing logit result
link_comparison <- rbind(
  Logit = cv14,
  Probit = cv_link("probit"),
  Cloglog = cv_link("cloglog")
)

print(link_comparison)
```

```{r}
average_precision <- function(y, p) {

  # Sort bookings from highest to lowest predicted risk
  ord <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)
  y <- y[ord]
  p <- p[ord]

  # Treat tied predicted probabilities together
  ends <- cumsum(rle(p)$lengths)

  # Cumulative true positives
  tp <- cumsum(y)[ends]

  # Precision and recall at each distinct threshold
  precision <- tp / ends
  recall <- tp / sum(y)

  # Average precision
  sum(
    c(recall[1], diff(recall)) * precision
  )
}

data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 11", "Model 14", "Prevalence baseline"),
  Average_Precision = c(
    average_precision(validation$is_canceled, p11),
    average_precision(validation$is_canceled, p14),
    mean(validation$is_canceled)
  )
)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

pr_curve <- function(y, p) {

  ord <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)
  y <- y[ord]
  p <- p[ord]

  # Handle tied probabilities together
  ends <- cumsum(rle(p)$lengths)

  tp <- cumsum(y)[ends]

  data.frame(
    Recall = c(0, tp / sum(y)),
    Precision = c(1, tp / ends)
  )
}

pr_data <- bind_rows(
  pr_curve(validation$is_canceled, p11) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Model 11"),

  pr_curve(validation$is_canceled, p14) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Model 14")
)

ggplot(
  pr_data,
  aes(x = Recall, y = Precision, colour = Model)
) +
  geom_step(direction = "vh") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = mean(validation$is_canceled),
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    ylim = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Precision–Recall Curves",
    subtitle = "Validation data",
    x = "Recall",
    y = "Precision",
    colour = "Model"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Evaluate Model 14 at different thresholds
thresholds <- c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7)

threshold_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(thresholds, function(t) {

  predicted_class <- as.integer(p14 >= t)
  actual <- validation$is_canceled

  TP <- sum(predicted_class == 1 & actual == 1)
  FP <- sum(predicted_class == 1 & actual == 0)
  FN <- sum(predicted_class == 0 & actual == 1)
  TN <- sum(predicted_class == 0 & actual == 0)

  data.frame(
    Threshold = t,
    Flagged = TP + FP,
    Precision = TP / (TP + FP),
    Recall = TP / (TP + FN),
    Specificity = TN / (TN + FP),
    Accuracy = (TP + TN) / length(actual),
    False_Positives = FP,
    Missed_Cancellations = FN
  )
}))

print(threshold_results)
```

# Prepare test predictors using the same transformations
test_export <- test

test_export$requests_group <- factor(
  pmin(test_export$total_of_special_requests, 3),
  levels = 0:3,
  labels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+")
)

test_export$prev_cancel_group <- factor(
  pmin(test_export$previous_cancellations, 2),
  levels = 0:2,
  labels = c("0", "1", "2+")
)

# Check for categorical values unseen in training
for (v in categorical_vars) {
  unseen <- setdiff(unique(test_export[[v]]),
                    unique(train[[v]]))
  if (length(unseen) > 0) {
    stop(paste("Unseen test category in", v,
               ":", paste(unseen, collapse = ", ")))
  }
}

# Predict probabilities, not 0/1 classes

  model14,
  newdata = test_export,
  type = "response"
))

  length(p_test14) == 17903,
